title: How many saplings were planted in the first week of July?
description: A bar graph shows the saplings planted by a school on each day of a week. The bars are added for two days and for the whole week, the greatest and least days are found, and reasons for the difference are thought about and checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: read each bar, add the readings, find the tallest and shortest bars, and give reasons that can be checked. Watch for students who add only some of the bars.

video_script.why: The child reads seven bars, adds some or all of them, finds the greatest and least bars, and gives reasons that can be checked.
video_script.substitution: Read each bar, add Wednesday and Thursday, add all seven days, then pick the tallest and shortest bars and think of reasons.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of saplings planted on each day of the first week of July: Monday 50, Tuesday 40, Wednesday 30, Thursday 40, Friday 50, Saturday 60, Sunday 40
video_script.payoff_line: The totals are seventy and three hundred and ten, with most on Saturday and least on Wednesday

final_answer.value: a. 70; b. 310; c. most on Saturday, least on Wednesday
final_answer.spoken: the totals are seventy and three hundred and ten, with most on Saturday and least on Wednesday

maths_rules: saplings planted: Monday 50, Tuesday 40, Wednesday 30, Thursday 40, Friday 50, Saturday 60, Sunday 40
c: greatest is Saturday, 60; least is Wednesday, 30
reasons are open: for example the rainy season or the number of students present
video_script.design: One idea: read the bars, add, compare, and then think of reasons that can be checked. The graph stays on the board all video. The reasons are open-ended, so the video gives the book's examples and says so.
open_questions: The bar values are read from the worklist, because the figure is not in the book text.
The question about reasons is open-ended. The video gives the book's example reasons, the rainy season and the number of students present, and does not claim they are the only ones.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the bar graph of saplings planted on each day of the week, Monday to Sunday, with a small tree sapling picture

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.graph: the bar graph of saplings planted on seven days appears
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the bars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about planting trees.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>Students and teachers of a school planted saplings on seven days. The bars show how many each day.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many were planted on two days, in the whole week, and why do the days differ?

beats.on_screen: the graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two bars labelled 20 and 30 saplings; a plus sign joins them and the total 50 saplings appears; the words read the top of the bar appear

marks.top: the top of each bar is lit and the words read the top of the bar appear
marks.plus: a plus sign joins the two bars

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>The top of a bar tells us the number for that day.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>To get the total of some days, add their numbers.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Twenty saplings on one day and thirty on another make fifty.

beats.on_screen: Given: Monday 50, Tuesday 40, Wednesday 30, Thursday 40, Friday 50, Saturday 60, Sunday 40 saplings

marks.first: Monday 50, Tuesday 40, Wednesday 30 and Thursday 40 are written
marks.last: Friday 50, Saturday 60 and Sunday 40 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the bars read fifty, forty, thirty and forty for Monday to Thursday.
<bookmark mark='last'/>They read fifty, sixty and forty for Friday to Sunday.

beats.on_screen: To find: a. Wednesday and Thursday together; b. the whole week; c. the greatest day, the least day, and reasons

marks.find: the three parts a, b and c are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two totals, the greatest and least days, and some reasons.

marks.two: the Wednesday bar 30 and the Thursday bar 40 are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step one, for the two days, read the bars of Wednesday and Thursday. They are thirty and forty.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Thirty and forty make seventy.

marks.pairs: the seven days are grouped as 50 + 40, 30 + 40, 50 + 60 and 40

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step two, for the whole week, add in pairs. Fifty and forty make ninety. Thirty and forty make seventy.
<bookmark mark='sixty'/>Fifty and sixty make one hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Ninety and seventy make one hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='end'/>One hundred and sixty and one hundred and ten make two hundred and seventy. Add the last forty, and we get three hundred and ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: c. the tallest bar is Saturday, 60; the shortest bar is Wednesday, 30

marks.tall: the Saturday bar, 60, is lit as the tallest
marks.short: the Wednesday bar, 30, is lit as the shortest

narration: <bookmark mark='tall'/>Step three, for the greatest and least days, compare the heights. The tallest bar is Saturday, with sixty.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The shortest bar is Wednesday, with thirty.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: possible reasons: it is the rainy season; the number of students present is different on different days; to check, ask the school and note the rain and the attendance on each day

marks.rain: a rain cloud appears over the Saturday bar
marks.students: a small crowd appears over Saturday and a small group over Wednesday
marks.check: a note pad with the words rain and attendance appears

narration: <bookmark mark='rain'/>Step four, think of reasons. The reasons here are open. One may be the rainy season, when planting is better.
<bookmark mark='students'/>Another may be that different numbers of students were present on different days.
<bookmark mark='check'/>To check, ask the school, and note the rain and the attendance on each day.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check in tens. 5 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 4 = 31 tens = 310; and 3 + 4 = 7 tens = 70

marks.tens: the bars are read in tens: 5, 4, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 4

narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Step five, check by reading the bars in tens. They are five, four, three, four, five, six and four.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>These add up to thirty one tens, which is three hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Three tens and four tens make seven tens, which is seventy. Both totals match.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. 70; b. 310; c. most on Saturday, least on Wednesday
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The totals are seventy and three hundred and ten, with most on Saturday and least on Wednesday.
